Turns a tailwind class list into an ElementStyle. Classes that are just a word ("flex", "italic") sit in KEYWORDS, the ones carrying a value ("p-4", "bg-red-500", "w-[120px]") sit in VALUED under their prefix, so adding a utility is one line. Anything the parser cannot use is handed back by parseInto, whether it is a class nothing knows at all or a known one carrying a value that makes no sense for it, so whatever called can say so.

A class can be written behind one or more `Variant`s, as "hover:bg-sky-500" is: those are read apart from the rest by `read`, which hands back a layer per set of variants for the element to put on while they hold.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.style.TailwindParser;
```

## Members

### `public static final int SPACING_UNIT = 4`

A tailwind spacing unit is 0.25rem; one unit to four gui pixels keeps the scale usable in game.

### `public record Problem(String className, Reason reason, String key)`

A class the parser could not use, and why.

### `public static ElementStyle parse(String classList)`

### `public static List<Problem> parseInto(ElementStyle.Builder style, String classList)`

Applies every class it can onto the builder and hands back the ones it could not. The classes behind a variant are read for whether they make sense, and so still say so when they do not, but their styles are dropped, since a builder has nowhere to keep the condition on them: use `read` to keep them.

### `public record Sheet(ElementStyle base, List<Layer> layers, List<Problem> problems)`

A class list read apart into the styles that are always there and the ones waiting on a variant. Every class with the same set of variants in front of it ends up in one layer, in the order the first of them was written, so a layer that comes later has the say over one that comes earlier.

### `public record Layer(Set<Variant> variants, long mask, ElementStyle style) {}`

Styles that only land while every variant in front of them holds, with that set of variants as one number as well, which is what an element tests against the variants it finds holding.
